[AMD] Do not insert barriers between mbarrier-synchronized TDM copies (#11896)

An async copy that carries an mbarrier operand sends an LDS atomic
arrive when it completes, so it takes part in mbarrier synchronization
exactly like AsyncCopyMbarrierArriveOp, which membarFilter already
recognizes. The mbarrier orders those accesses across the whole
workgroup, so a ttg.barrier between two such ops synchronizes nothing.

Copies without a barrier operand are deliberately not covered here.
Those are ordered by their async wait instead, and an async wait counter
is per wave, so it cannot order accesses between waves.

Without this, a TDM collective expressed with mbarrier completion emits
more barriers than the async_tdm_wait formulation it replaces, which
makes mbarrier unusable as an alternative.

[AMD][Gluon] Add Gluon example for CDNA5 clustered warp-pipeline GEMMs (#12073)

## Summary
Add high-performance examples of 8-wave GEMM kernel

  Supported operand combinations:

  - **BF16 × BF16** (`--dtype bf16`)
- **MXFP8 × MXFP8** (`--dtype mxfp8`): FP8 E4M3 operands with E8M0 block
scales.
- **MXFP4 × MXFP4** (`--dtype mxfp4`): FP4 E2M1 operands with E8M0 block
scales.
- **FP8 × MXFP4** (`--dtype fp8_mxfp4`): unscaled FP8 E4M3 A and FP4
E2M1 B with E8M0 block scales.
  - **All four variants** (`--dtype all`, the default).

All kernels use FP32 accumulation and BF16 output. TDM transfers
multicast operands into shared memory.

BF16 uses a two-tile unrolled load/compute/refill schedule. The three
scaled variants use five-stage pipelines with delayed cluster waits,
six-tile main-loop unrolling, and cleanup/drain handling.

MXFP8 supports explicit CTA tile and CGA cluster selection. An optional
two-buffer output epilogue overlaps the BK256 output stores. Matrix
dimensions are supplied through the CLI, and unsupported configurations
are rejected.

The example includes reference correctness checks and GPU graph
benchmarking, with optional rotation through distinct input/output
allocations. Input generation, compilation, and correctness checking are
excluded from timing.

  ## Command-line options

  ### Kernel configuration

- `--dtype {all,bf16,mxfp8,mxfp4,fp8_mxfp4}`: kernel variant; default
`all`.
  - `-M`, `-N`, `-K`: matrix dimensions.
- `--mxfp8-tile {256x256x256,128x128x512,64x64x512}`: MXFP8 CTA tile;
required when running MXFP8, including with `--dtype all`.
- `--mxfp8-cluster {2x2,4x4}`: MXFP8 CGA cluster; required when running
MXFP8.
- `--mxfp8-output-buffers {1,2}`: output LDS buffer count; default `1`.
Two buffers require the BK256 MXFP8 tile.
- `--flat-pipeline`: fully unroll the loop including tail so compiler
can fully optimize it. Only supports mxfp8 for now.

  ### Inputs and correctness

- `--input {auto,random,trig,positive_mxfp8}`: input generation mode;
default `auto`. `--input-mode` is an alias.
  - `--seed`: random seed; default `42`.
- `--check`: verify output against a reference. Enabled automatically
when neither checking nor benchmarking is requested.

`auto` selects trig inputs for BF16, MXFP8, and MXFP4, and random inputs
for FP8 × MXFP4. `positive_mxfp8` generates positive FP8 values and E8M0
scales and requires `--dtype mxfp8`.

  ### Benchmarking

  - `--benchmark`: measure kernel execution using GPU graphs.
  - `--warmup`: warmup launches; default `20`.
- `--rotate-inputs`: benchmark distinct copies of operands, scales, and
output. Disabled by default; implies `--benchmark`.
- `--repeats`: total timed launches with rotation; default `100`, range
`1–200`.
  - `--samples`: timing samples; default `4`. Rotation requires `1`.
- `--replays`: graph replays per sample; default `20`. Rotation requires
`1`.
- `--iters-per-graph`: launches per graph; default `50`. With rotation,
must equal `--repeats`.
  - `-h`, `--help`: display usage and option descriptions.

  ## Validation

- Correctness checks for all four data-type combinations and all
supported MXFP8 tile/cluster combinations.
  - Positive input values and scales match the archived generator.
- One- and two-buffer MXFP8 output epilogues produce bitwise-identical
results.
  - Python syntax, formatting, and whitespace checks passed.

+
+Each kernel uses eight warps per CTA, FP32 accumulation and BF16 output.
+BF16, MXFP4 and FP8 x MXFP4 use a 4x4 CTA cluster (1024x1024 output tile).
+MXFP8 supports 2x2/4x4 clusters and 64/128/256-square CTA tiles. TDM multicasts
+operands into LDS.

+* BF16: BK128, two data slots and an unroll-2 load/compute/refill schedule.
+* MXFP8: BK256 with CTA256 (two data/three scale slots), or BK512 with
+  CTA64/128 (two data/scale slots); five stages and six-tile unroll.
+* MXFP4: BK512, two data slots and three scale slots, six-tile unroll.
+* FP8 x MXFP4: BK256, three slots each for A, B and B scales, six-tile unroll.
+
+The three scaled kernels use five stages with phase gap one:
+load low -> compute low -> load high/arrive/advance -> compute high
+-> wait/refill.
+Leading refill overlaps trailing compute after its LDS reads have completed.
+TDM readiness waits and warp-pipeline boundaries protect buffer lifetimes;
+cluster arrive/wait are scheduling hints. B reuse is not enabled here.
+
+Run from this directory on CDNA5, for example::
+
+    python gemm_warp_pipeline_cdna5.py --dtype all --check \
+        --mxfp8-tile 256x256x256 --mxfp8-cluster 4x4
+    python gemm_warp_pipeline_cdna5.py --dtype mxfp8 --check --benchmark \
+        --mxfp8-tile 128x128x512 --mxfp8-cluster 4x4
+

+
+    python gemm_warp_pipeline_cdna5.py --dtype mxfp8 \
+        --rotate-inputs --repeats 100 \
+        --mxfp8-tile 256x256x256 --mxfp8-cluster 4x4

+addresses. It times one graph replay containing --repeats launches (default 100,
+maximum 200), per dtype, excluding warmup. Samples and replays must both be one.

+def _trig_scale_chunks(rows, k):
+    """Yield value bits and block-32 scales matching hipBLASLt's trig generator.
+
+    Preserve its 32 independently seeded MT19937 streams, contiguous block
+    ranges, and libstdc++ double generation order. Chunking bounds memory use.
+    """
+    if k % 32:
+        raise ValueError('MXFP trig generation requires K divisible by 32')
+    block_size = 32
+    num_threads = 32
+    blocks = rows * k // block_size
+    if blocks % num_threads:
+        raise ValueError('MXFP trig generation requires scale blocks divisible by 32')
+    blocks_per_thread = blocks // num_threads
+    blocks_per_chunk = 32 * 1024
+    output_block = 0
+    for thread in range(num_threads):
+        rng = np.random.RandomState(TRIG_SEED + thread)
+        remaining = blocks_per_thread
+        while remaining:
+            chunk_blocks = min(remaining, blocks_per_chunk)
+            count = chunk_blocks * block_size
+            # Match libstdc++ generate_canonical<double, 53>: low word first.
+            raw = rng.randint(0, 2**32, size=(count, 2), dtype=np.uint32)
+            uniform = (raw[:, 0].astype(np.float64) + raw[:, 1].astype(np.float64) * 2.0**32) * 2.0**(-64)
+            bits = np.cos(uniform * (2.0 * np.pi)).view(np.uint64).reshape(chunk_blocks, block_size)
+            exponent = (bits >> 52 & 2047).astype(np.int32) - 1023
+            element_scales = np.maximum(exponent, -127) + 127
+            block_scales = np.floor(element_scales.mean(axis=1) + 0.5).astype(np.int32)
+            adjusted = element_scales - block_scales[:, None]
+            yield output_block, bits, adjusted, block_scales.astype(np.uint8)
+            output_block += chunk_blocks
+            remaining -= chunk_blocks
+

+def _make_mxfp8_trig_matrix(rows, k):
+    """Encode trig inputs as E4M3 values with E8M0 block scales."""
+    data = torch.empty((rows, k), dtype=torch.uint8)
+    scales = torch.empty((rows, k // 32), dtype=torch.uint8)
+    data_flat = data.numpy().reshape(-1)
+    scale_flat = scales.numpy().reshape(-1)
+    for output_block, bits, adjusted, block_scales in _trig_scale_chunks(rows, k):
+        sign = (bits >> 63 << 7).astype(np.uint8)
+        mantissa = ((bits & (1 << 52) - 1) >> 49).astype(np.uint8)
+        encoded = np.zeros(bits.shape, dtype=np.uint8)
+        normal = adjusted >= -6
+        encoded[normal] = sign[normal] | (adjusted[normal] + 7).astype(np.uint8) << 3 | mantissa[normal]
+        subnormal = (adjusted >= -9) & (adjusted < -6)
+        subnormal_mantissa = mantissa[subnormal] >> 1 | 4
+        subnormal_mantissa >>= (-7 - adjusted[subnormal]).astype(np.uint8)
+        encoded[subnormal] = sign[subnormal] | subnormal_mantissa
+        data_begin = output_block * 32
+        data_flat[data_begin:data_begin + encoded.size] = encoded.reshape(-1)
+        scale_flat[output_block:output_block + block_scales.size] = block_scales
+    return (data, scales)

+def _make_mxfp4_trig_matrix(rows, k):
+    """Encode trig inputs as E2M1 values with E8M0 block scales."""
+    data = torch.empty((rows, k), dtype=torch.uint8)
+    scales = torch.empty((rows, k // 32), dtype=torch.uint8)
+    data_flat = data.numpy().reshape(-1)
+    scale_flat = scales.numpy().reshape(-1)
+    for output_block, bits, adjusted, block_scales in _trig_scale_chunks(rows, k):
+        sign = (bits >> 63 << 3).astype(np.uint8)
+        mantissa = ((bits & (1 << 52) - 1) >> 51).astype(np.uint8)
+        encoded = np.zeros(bits.shape, dtype=np.uint8)
+        normal = adjusted >= 0
+        encoded[normal] = sign[normal] | np.minimum((adjusted[normal] + 1) * 2 + mantissa[normal], 7).astype(np.uint8)
+        subnormal = adjusted == -1
+        encoded[subnormal] = sign[subnormal] | 1
+        data_begin = output_block * 32
+        data_flat[data_begin:data_begin + encoded.size] = encoded.reshape(-1)
+        scale_flat[output_block:output_block + block_scales.size] = block_scales
+    return (data, scales)

[Standard] Add any/all reductions (#12129)

This adds a convenience helper for doing any/all reductions. Lots of
existing code does `tl.sum(pred) != 0` for any, but it turns out that
the min/max redux operations are more efficient than the add operation
so this results in higher latency:

Elements | Min/max, ns/iteration | Sum, ns/iteration | Speedup
-- | -- | -- | --
32 | 22.6 | 36.6 | 1.62×
128 | 57.4 | 81.8 | 1.43×
512 | 71.0 | 102.5 | 1.44×
2048 | 110.2 | 140.7 | 1.28×
8192 | 265.8 | 283.7 | 1.07×

Building the faster method into the stdlib should encourage its use more
broadly.

[Analysis] Speed up buffer-view deduplication (#12085)

## Summary

Replace ordered buffer-view deduplication with a hash set. This avoids
repeated address-set comparisons used only to order views. Each stored
view caches a full hash of its metadata, cooperative thread array (CTA)
IDs, and exact address sets. Matching hashes still require full
equality.

`BufferRegionView` stores its full-content hash in a private
`std::optional`, computed on first use by the hash set. All equality
fields are const, so the cached value cannot become stale. Translation
and subview construction produce new values with empty caches; copies
preserve the cache. Equality can reject different cached hashes
immediately, but matching hashes still require full comparison.
`RegionInfo` uses copy-and-swap assignment for libc++ compatibility with
immutable elements. Diagnostics and emitted sanitizer cases are sorted
for deterministic output.

Hash collisions can still require O(n²) equality checks across n
insertions; ordered-set insertion requires O(n log n) ordering
comparisons.

## Desired features

- Deduplicate buffer views without per-insertion address-set ordering.
- Lazily cache full-content hashes inside immutable buffer views.

## Validation

NVIDIA GB300 / Linux AArch64; two fresh-process, empty-cache runs per
workload, with line information disabled. Previously recorded mean
compilation times, before this immutable-view refactor: **1.482 s**
synthetic, **10.346 s** for 15 tutorial/example compilations, and
**49.578 s** for the 135-compilation sweep. Synthetic timing covers cold
compilation; tutorial timing sums compiler-listener measurements.

Validation includes native analysis tests and compiler regressions on
macOS (Apple Clang/libc++) and Linux AArch64 (GCC/libstdc++), plus
focused Concurrency Sanitizer (ConSan) GPU tests on NVIDIA GB300.
Performance benchmarks were not rerun for this immutable-view refactor.
Earlier benchmark runs matched GPU test outcomes and compiled binaries;
early source/IR names matched after normalizing Python object addresses.

### Recorded master comparison

**These historical benchmark and profile tables predate cached
full-content hashing; their PR columns do not measure the current
head.** Master is `dd7167259f38`; LLVM is `b010a18d2b64`. Times are
seconds; two cold runs per individual workload and one per compiler for
the 135-compilation sweep.

| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Synthetic stress case | 70.308 | 1.453 | 48.40x |
| Overlapping accumulator | 2.325 | 0.663 | 3.51x |
| Multi-CTA tutorial | 1.477 | 0.624 | 2.37x |
| Attention | 6.531 | 3.707 | 1.76x |
| 135-compilation tutorial/example sweep | 72.545 | 50.545 | 1.44x |

**Recorded profile highlights — time and share of compilation:**

| Cost | Synthetic stress case | 15 tutorial/example kernels |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Equality | 52.0 ms (3.55%) | 17.5 ms (0.17%) |
| Copying | 366.8 ms (25.04%) | 135.2 ms (1.33%) |

| All measured analysis operations | 472.6 ms (32.25%) | 532.1 ms
(5.22%) |

Profile: `bf5bb5373058`, excluding nested double-counting; timer

representations and PTX. Historical hash-variant checks matched binaries
and LLVM IR across 30 focused and 270 broad compilation pairs.

Recorded native collision stress before the move optimization: 4,096

## Lines Changed

| Type | Added | Removed | Net |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Tests | 133 | 7 | 126 |
| Core Logic | 110 | 38 | 72 |
| AutoGenerated | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Total | 243 | 45 | 198 |

## Synthetic benchmark

This kernel repeatedly merges two equal shared-memory footprints across
128 unrolled branches. It deliberately exaggerates comparison cost,
rather than representing a typical workload.

Measured with `WIDTH=131072`, `STEPS=128`, `CTAS=8`, `STAGES=1`,
`num_warps=4`, `num_ctas=8`, and `grid=(1,)`. The first two `flags`
entries are zero; the remaining entries are runtime booleans. Timing
covers cold compilation; GPU execution is checked afterward (all 128
outputs must equal 9).

<details>
<summary>Synthetic kernel</summary>

```python
from triton.experimental import gluon as g
from triton.experimental.gluon import language as gl

@g.jit
def descriptor_swap(flags, out, WIDTH: gl.constexpr, STEPS: gl.constexpr, CTAS: gl.constexpr, STAGES: gl.constexpr):
    cga: gl.constexpr = [[0]] * (CTAS.bit_length() - 1)
    layout: gl.constexpr = gl.BlockedLayout([1], [32], [4], [0], cga_layout=cga)
    parent = gl.allocate_shared_memory(gl.int8, [STAGES, WIDTH], gl.SwizzledSharedLayout(1, 1, 1, [0], cga_layout=cga))
    for stage in gl.static_range(STAGES):
        parent.index(stage).slice(0, 128).store(gl.full([128], 3 + 4 * stage, gl.int8, layout))
    ia = gl.load(flags)
    ib = gl.load(flags + 1)
    if STAGES != 1:
        ia = ia % STAGES
        ib = ib % STAGES
    a = parent.index(ia)
    b = parent.index(ib)
    for i in gl.static_range(STEPS):
        cond = gl.load(flags + 2 + i) != 0
        if cond:
            a, b = b, a
    x = a.slice(0, 128).load(layout)
    y = b.slice(0, 128).load(layout)
    gl.store(out + gl.arange(0, 128, layout=layout), x.to(gl.int32) + 2 * y.to(gl.int32))
```

</details>

- `include/triton/Analysis/BufferRegion.h`: immutable view fields, lazy
hash cache, hash-set storage, and deterministic printing.
- `lib/Analysis/BufferRegion.cpp`: full-content hashing and construction
of translated views and subviews.
- `lib/Dialect/TritonInstrument/IR/Utility.cpp`: sorts `(baseOffset,
ctaMask)` cases for deterministic ConSan output.
- `test/lib/Analysis/TestBufferRegion.cpp`: constructs views with their
allocation frame.
- `unittest/Analysis/UtilityTest.cpp` and
`test/Analysis/test-membar.mlir`: equality/collision, immutable
cached-hash, container assignment, and barrier regressions.

There are no movement-only files.

[Optimizer] Remove reshape reduction reordering pattern (#12124)

Reshape operands of a multi-operand reduction or a masked histogram must
preserve their elementwise correspondence.
`CombineReshapeReducePatterns` independently marks one-dimensional
reshapes as `allow_reorder`, which can break that correspondence. Remove
the pattern and its registration, and update the existing combine test
to check that reshape order is preserved.

The layout-conversion tests cover ordered reshapes feeding single- and
multi-operand scalar reductions, plus plain and masked histograms. They
check that `remove_layout_conversions` eliminates the input/output
conversions while preserving element order and operand correspondence,
without running `triton-combine`.

## Validation

Monorepo CI tested compiler commit `becbd4eb85`, based directly on the
OpenAI monorepo's Triton pin, `fa8415bdf8`. Commit `314f33c59b` adds
only the lit coverage described below; the compiler change is unchanged.

(internal), via the [Triton wheel pin
update](https://github.com/openai/openai/pull/1654370), reports
**success**. 2,302 jobs passed, including the non-quarantined KI
correctness and runtime-performance checks. All seven initially blocking
timeout failures passed on retry; no confirmed correctness or
runtime-performance regression was found.

had non-blocking timeouts, and the optional async/personal suites were
not run.

(2 unsupported), and all 20 focused reshape/histogram GPU tests passed.
- With the added cases, `test/TritonGPU/combine.mlir` passes on Brix
GB300 using the previously built compiler and the verified updated test
source. The run invokes only `tritongpu-remove-layout-conversions` and
CSE.

[PROTON][triton-ext] Allow registering a backend at runtime (#12118)

Closes #12048

Proton backends can only be registered at build time, through
`TRITON_PLUGIN_DIRS` (#10246). A backend shipped as its own package
against an already built Triton cannot add its profiler, device and
runtime.

This adds `proton::registerBackend()`. The backend's library calls it
when it is loaded, for example from the package Triton imports through
the `triton.backends` entry point, so no new discovery mechanism is
needed.

- Runtime registrations go into the same registry as the build-time
ones, after them, so every existing query sees them and build-time
backends keep priority. Build-time registration is unchanged.
- The device of such a backend uses the new `DeviceType::EXTERNAL`.
There is one such value, so one runtime-registered backend per process.
**_(Should there be more slots in advance?)_**
- The msgpack dump now takes device type names from the registrations
instead of looking up every value up to `COUNT`, so an unused `EXTERNAL`
needs no name.
- `registerBackend` is resolved from `libproton`, so this needs a build
with `TRITON_EXT_ENABLED`, as the official wheels are.

Tested with a new case in `BackendRegistrationTest`, and end to end with
a profiler built as a separate library and registered this way. Profiler
selection, the `proton` CLI in a child process, and hatchet and msgpack
output work as they do with a profiler built into Proton.

@Jokeren @GeorgeWigley @abrown

 extension points it supports. Backend implementations should follow the existing
 `CuptiProfiler` and `RoctracerProfiler` patterns for callback correlation,
 runtime events, and metric insertion.
+
+### Registering at runtime
+
+A backend shipped separately from Triton, for example in its own package, can
+register when its library is loaded instead. It passes the same
+`BackendRegistration` to `proton::registerBackend` before profiling starts, with
+`proton::DeviceType::EXTERNAL` as the device type. For now there is a single
+`DeviceType::EXTERNAL`, so a process can have only one device type registered
+this way.

+```c++
+__attribute__((constructor)) static void registerMyBackend() {
+  proton::registerBackend(makeMyBackendRegistration());
+}
+```
+
+The library resolves `registerBackend` from `libproton`, so Triton has to be
+built with `TRITON_EXT_ENABLED`, as the official wheels are.

This PR adds multi-cta support to the simpler scheduling variants:

Schedule | M split | N split | M×N split
-- | -- | -- | --
baseline | Yes | Yes | Yes

sliceNK | Yes | No | No

The missing variants will be added in a followup PR. They require
reshapes/permutes so it's easier to review if they are in a separate PR.
